wiktionary.gloss: A set A such that every element of A is also an element of S.

examples: We asked a subset of the population of the town for their opinion.
wiktionary.gloss: A group of things or people, all of which are in a specified larger group.

blocks.etymology: From sub- + set.

senses.definition: To select a smaller group of data or items from a larger collection.

examples.en: We can subset the table to analyze results by region.
examples.vi: Chúng ta có thể trích tập con của bảng để phân tích kết quả theo vùng.

senses.vi: chia nhỏ dữ liệu; trích xuất tập con

wiktionary.gloss: To take a subset of.
To extract only the portions of (a font) that are needed to display a particular document.

senses.definition: made by a tailor or fitted well to the shape of a person's body

examples.en: He wore an expensive tailored suit to the interview.
examples.vi: Anh ấy mặc một bộ com-lê may đo đắt tiền đến buổi phỏng vấn.

thesaurus.definition: severely simple in line or design
(of clothing) custom-made

wiktionary.gloss: Adjusted by a tailor, fitted.

examples: His expensive tailored shirts didn't look that much better than off-the-rack, but they lasted much longer.
wiktionary.gloss: Made by a tailor.
Any of several steaks cut from the tenderest part of the loin of beef.

blocks.etymology: From tow + line.

thesaurus.definition: (nautical) a rope used in towing

examples: Near-synonym: towrope
wiktionary.gloss: A line (e.g., manila rope, wire rope, woven polymer strap) used for towing a vehicle (e.g., motor vehicle, marine vessel).

blocks.etymology: The adjective and noun are derived from Middle English truant, truand, truaund (“(adjective) idle; tending to vagrancy (uncertain; may be a use of the noun); (noun) beggar; mendicant friar; vagrant, wanderer; worthless person, rogue, scoundrel; one who is absent without leave, truant; one who shirks duties”), from Old French truant, truand (“(adjective) beggarly; roguish; (noun) a beggar, vagabond; a rogue”) (modern French truand), probably of Celtic origin, possibly from Gaulish *trugan, or from Breton truan (“wretched”), from Proto-Celtic *taratrom, from Proto-Indo-European *térh₁-tro-m, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to drill, pierce; to rub; to turn”). Cognates

thesaurus.definition: absent without permission

vi_block: Hay trốn học, hay trốn việc; lêu lổng; lười biếng.

wiktionary.gloss: Shirking or wandering from business or duty; straying; hence, idle; loitering.

examples: He didn’t graduate because he was chronically truant and didn’t have enough attendances to meet the requirement.
wiktionary.gloss: Of a student: absent from school without permission.

blocks.etymology: The adjective and noun are derived from Middle English truant, truand, truaund (“(adjective) idle; tending to vagrancy (uncertain; may be a use of the noun); (noun) beggar; mendicant friar; vagrant, wanderer; worthless person, rogue, scoundrel; one who is absent without leave, truant; one who shirks duties”), from Old French truant, truand (“(adjective) beggarly; roguish; (noun) a beggar, vagabond; a rogue”) (modern French truand), probably of Celtic origin, possibly from Gaulish *trugan, or from Breton truan (“wretched”), from Proto-Celtic *taratrom, from Proto-Indo-European *térh₁-tro-m, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to drill, pierce; to rub; to turn”). Cognates

thesaurus.definition: one who is absent from school without permission
someone who shirks duty

wiktionary.gloss: An idle or lazy person; an idler.
A student who is absent from school without permission; hence (figurative), a person who shirks or wanders from business or duty.

blocks.etymology: Inherited from Middle English truaunten (“to obtain alms fraudulently; to behave like a rogue or scoundrel; to neglect a duty; to be idle or lazy”), and then partly: * from Old French truander (modern French truander (“to cheat, to con”)), from truand (noun) (see etymology 1) + -er (suffix forming infinitives of first-conjugation verbs); and
vi_block: Trốn học, trốn việc; lêu lông.

examples: The number of schoolchildren known to have truanted from this school has been unusually high.
wiktionary.gloss: Also used with the impersonal pronoun it (dated): to shirk or wander from business or duty; (specifically) of a student: to be absent from school without permission; to play truant.

blocks.etymology: Proto-Indo-European *n̥- From un- + awed.

wiktionary.gloss: Not awed; not afraid, impressed, or in awe.

blocks.etymology: Mixed metaphor combining until the cows come home + when hell freezes over.

wiktionary.gloss: For a very long period of time.

examples: It's nice to be able to look back on the thing, because I was so up my own ass at the time about everything that it was hard to enjoy all the craziness...
wiktionary.gloss: Having an excessively high opinion of oneself, excessively preoccupied with one's own affairs, or lost in self-regarding abstraction.
